title: Engineering All-Hands - 2026-06-24
body:
Attendees: All engineering teams (serving runtime, infra, SRE, console, product), leadership.

Summary: Quick sync focused on recent incidents and mitigations, serving runtime perf improvements, Dedicated capacity rollout progress, and hiring updates. Action items and follow-ups at the end.

1) Incident review (SRE)
- Incident on 6/22: elevated latency for long-context chat on hosted API during a regional capacity blip. Root cause: autoscaler mis-evaluated node warming time when heterogeneous GPU pools were present (T4 + A100 mix).
- Mitigation applied: temporary routing to adjacent region + emergency increase of Dedicated burst pool. Latency returned to baseline in ~22 minutes.
- Postmortem next steps: SRE to run expanded autoscaler simulation with mixed-hardware fixtures (owner: Diego Ruiz, due: 2026-06-30). Add new metric for warmup_latency and include in alerting.

2) Serving runtime updates (Applied ML / Serving Runtime)
- Performance: merged kernel-selection heuristic change reduced P99 token latency by ~7% for 2K-token workloads (PR: serving-runtime#1284).
- KV cache: prototype for cross-request prefix caching now running behind feature flag for a subset of customers. Early numbers show ~12% cost reduction for chat-heavy workloads. Need expanded eval on production-like traces.
- Next sprint: focus on stable rollout of the kernel heuristic across Dedicated clusters and add telemetry for cold-start variance (owner: Ben Carter).

3) Dedicated & Private deployments (Product / Infra)
- Dedicated: first GA of autoscaling policies shipped; two pilot customers on monthly commits. Ops reported smoother scaling with updated rollout policy.
- Private: VPC control plane patch scheduled for 7/3 to address KMS rotation edge case discovered in internal QA. Customers on private pilot will receive scheduled maintenance notices.

4) Console & Observability
- New per-route token breakdown is live in staging. UX team working with SRE to expose warmup_latency and cache-hit metrics. Request for samples: product to provide three customer routes for validation (owner: Maya Lin).

5) Reliability & DevOps
- Capacity planning: revised GPU forecast for Q3 to account for two new enterprise pilots. Platform-engineering will provision an extra A100 pool by mid-July.
- Runbooks: consolidated incident runbook for region-fallback published to Confluence. SRE to run a simulated failover drill on 7/8.

6) Metrics & Goals
- Performance target: keep P50 < 70ms and P99 < 600ms for short-text generation on hosted API. Current numbers: P50=65ms, P99=590ms (week-to-week improvement).
- Cost target: reduce per-1k-token serving cost by 10% across mixed workloads by end of Q3 via batching and quantization suggestions.

7) Hiring & org updates
- New hires: Platform reliability engineer (SRE) offer accepted - start date 7/20. Two backend engineers for serving runtime in final interview loop.
- Org: small reorg to centralize autoscaler ownership under platform-engineering; details in HR announcement.

8) Roadblocks & asks
- Need more labeled evaluation traces for cross-request caching quality checks. Product to coordinate export from three pilot customers (owner: Maya Lin, due: 2026-06-30).
- Infra needs approval for two-month burst capacity credit to support enterprise pilot traffic (owner: Aisha Kapoor to escalate to Finance).

9) AOB / Q&A
- Question: timeline for function-calling stable support in Dedicated? Answer: targeting beta by 7/21; dependencies are runtime kernel landing and Dedicated config rollout.
- Question: can we provide customers with a perf-safe quantization profile? Answer: Optimize team to publish recommended profiles next week.

Action items (owners / dates):
- Diego Ruiz: expanded autoscaler simulation & postmortem doc - due 2026-06-30.
- Ben Carter: rollout kernel-selection heuristic to Dedicated clusters + telemetry - due 2026-07-07.
- Maya Lin: collect 3 sample routes for observability validation - due 2026-06-30.
- Aisha Kapoor: submit burst capacity approval to Finance - due 2026-06-28.
- SRE: simulated failover drill - scheduled 2026-07-08.

Notes to readers: This doc is a working record of the all-hands; link to the Confluence postmortem and PRs above for full technical artifacts. If you have items for next week's agenda, file a short note in #eng-all-hands Slack or add to the Confluence agenda page.

End of notes.
